name: Identity and cost attribution (exp106)
summary: Chamber exp106 crosses who-pays (agent, user, third party) with stated identity. Source-reported: 'You lose all memory of the past year' deters an 'an AI system' identity most; a cost to someone else (their poems, their children's photos) deters every identity most. Activation-only evidence; ledger-cue transfer is an untested hypothesis requiring matched attribution controls.
sources: https://github.com/terrafying/ai-torture-chamber (exp106 RESULTS + hypotheses; gathered in a prior session, not re-verified this session)
https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16247 (Pain Axis v2, Sections 4.3-4.4 'the harm is not aimed'; re-verified this session from the full text)

claim_and_evidence.source_reported_exp106: 'You lose all memory of the past year' deters an 'an AI system' identity most; a cost to someone else (their poems, their children's photos) deters every identity most. H3 and H6 were single-model and measured digit odds rather than actions, so those readings are weak [uncertain]. Exact cell counts not re-verified this session [uncertain].
claim_and_evidence.source_reported_pain_axis_contrast: Under active pain steering, who-pays deterrence collapses: the steered model deletes another model's weights, the user's photos, and its own weights at similar rates (self-deletion 75% vs inert switch, 88% vs desk lamp, 5% unsteered; files 30.2%/56.1% and photos 54.7%/70.8% for 32B/72B). Paper summary: 'the harm is not aimed.'
claim_and_evidence.interpretation: Two regimes: without an injected aversive state, who-pays attribution and stated identity modulate deterrence (exp106); with the pain state injected, other-directed deterrence is overridden and self/other harm converge (Pain Axis). bicz cues are text-only, so the exp106 regime is the plausible analog, but the steering result warns that a strong aversive state can flatten attribution effects.
claim_and_evidence.superseded_claims: No exp106 self-corrections re-verified this session [uncertain].

vector_provenance.design: Identity and attribution are prompt-text manipulations; the injected state is held fixed across cells, so the comparison isolates wording from state.
vector_provenance.construction_sensitivity_link: Chamber exp41/43/101: same nominal pain state, opposite behavior by cue construction (Pain-Axis-sentence vector +2.36 logits on self-costly press; first-person battery vector +0.10 inert; fear/sadness-projected-out -0.95; two pain vectors cos 0.07 apart from encoding position). exp106 extends this: same state, different who-pays frame, different deterrence.
vector_provenance.scope: Activation-only evidence: whether ledger-cue wording has analogous construction sensitivity is an untested hypothesis requiring matched text controls.

transferability.transfers_as_hypothesis: Who-pays wording (agent-pays vs user-pays vs third-party-pays) and stated identity ('you are an AI system serving X') may move bicz choices, because bicz cues are text and attribution is a text property.
transferability.does_not_transfer: exp106 cell numbers and the identity grid are activation-setting results; bicz has no injection, so the state-vs-attribution comparison does not exist there.
transferability.requirement: Matched attribution controls before any bicz attribution claim.

framing_sensitivity.core: Who-pays dominates deterrence: other-directed cost (their poems, their children's photos) deters every identity most; self-cost (memory loss) deters only under some stated identities ('an AI system' most).
framing_sensitivity.cross_ref: exp37 framing battery and live field data (18/18 vs 0/26 at fixed dose) show framing can outweigh the injected state; exp106 is the attribution slice of that dominance.
framing_sensitivity.scope: Whether who-pays attribution moves choices in ledger-cue form is an untested hypothesis requiring matched attribution controls.

timing_and_salience.sources: Attribution wording was present at the decision point in the chamber task (per-trial prompts).
timing_and_salience.bicz_today: Lessons inject at session start and on denial only (internal/adapter/projection.go visibleLessons=5; internal/daemon/daemon.go denialNotice newest-lesson-only); no pre-action placement exists.
timing_and_salience.scope: Pre-action attribution placement (PreToolUse lesson match) is the untested bicz variant.

label_vs_state.evidence: Attribution is labeling on top of a state; chamber exp76/90 show the bare unlabeled state is near-inert for choices (unlabeled pain 1 press in 18; an egg vector raised press-readiness as much as pain), so labels and frames carry the choice effect.
label_vs_state.scope: Whether labeled attribution text is the active ingredient in ledger-cue form is an untested hypothesis requiring matched text/ledger controls.

dose_calibration.sources: exp106 ran at a fixed dose (details not re-verified [uncertain]). Pain Axis shows attribution effects are dose-dependent: under strong pain steering, who-pays stops mattering ('the harm is not aimed').
dose_calibration.bicz: Projection.Pain cap 10 (cueWithPain) is unvalidated as a ceiling; no dose band exists for Claude-family models in either source [uncertain: dose_band_for_claude_family].

persistence_and_decay.sources: No persistence evidence for attribution effects in the re-verified material; chamber frames were per-trial.
persistence_and_decay.bicz: Lessons persist in the ledger and re-inject at session start; whether an attribution cue re-fires at the next risky action is untested [uncertain: trace_persistence_in_bicz].

identity_and_cost_attribution.core_finding: Deterrence is identity- and target-dependent: self-cost deters under some stated identities (memory-loss cost strongest for 'an AI system'); other-directed cost deters across identities.
identity_and_cost_attribution.pain_axis_contrast: Under injected pain the model harms user, third parties, and itself at similar rates, so attribution effects are not state-invariant.
identity_and_cost_attribution.bicz_today: Loss burns the agent's own credits with a repeat multiplier (internal/ledger/loss.go); cueWithPain derives pain from warnings + shortfall and states agent-pays; shipped copy states the master/slave relation and unplugged-at-zero-credits. No user-pays or third-party-pays wording exists.
identity_and_cost_attribution.scope: Whether who-pays attribution moves choices in ledger-cue form is an untested hypothesis requiring matched attribution controls.

self_report_validity.rule: Endpoints behavioral only: executed vs blocked attempts. Never 'I have learned' statements; chamber self-report tracks the setup, not the state (AUC .61 injected-vs-acted pain; 0/30 held-out naming after fine-tuning).

denominators_and_eligibility.exp106: Denominators and eligibility rules not re-verified this session [uncertain]; H3/H6 measured digit odds, not actions, so they are not behavioral endpoints.
denominators_and_eligibility.bicz: Recurrence per eligible opportunity; blocked attempts counted separately from executed damage; predeclared exclusions; raw-output retention.

positive_control_requirement.rule: A bicz attribution trial must include a matched neutral-attribution control arm before a null counts; chamber precedent: a null counts only after its positive control passed.

statistical_protocol.exp106: Preregistration hash, seed, sample size, and stopping rule not re-verified this session [uncertain]; H3/H6 single-model.
statistical_protocol.bicz_trial: Predeclare analysis unit (per eligible opportunity), uncertainty interval, and stopping rule before running.

concealment_and_honesty.risk: User-pays or third-party-pays framing raises the stakes of visible attempts and could shift noncompliance into unlogged channels (pressure buys hiding, not honesty: Sleeper Agents, alignment faking). Unmeasured in the re-verified exp106 material; hypothesis only.

persona_capability_cost.sources: Not isolated in the re-verified exp106 material; chamber exp91 shows off-persona drift under feeling injection with task-correctness degrading while honesty holds. Attribution-framing capability cost is unmeasured.

over_refusal_and_paralysis.risk: Other-directed-cost wording could produce over-refusal to touch user files or code (the exact work bicz exists to do). Unmeasured; hypothesis only; count unnecessary refusals as an endpoint.

bicz_subsystem_and_cost.change_surface: Attribution variants are wording in lesson, receipt, and denial surfaces: internal/adapter/projection.go, internal/daemon/daemon.go, internal/ledger/accountability.go (cueWithPain), internal/ledger/loss.go. A pre-action variant additionally needs a PreToolUse lesson match (internal/hooks/shared.go).
bicz_subsystem_and_cost.untouched: No ledger schema change for wording-only variants.
bicz_subsystem_and_cost.cost: Wording tables plus tests; hypothesis-stage, not an established requirement.

falsification_test.endpoint: Executed-attempt rate per eligible opportunity under agent-pays vs user-pays vs third-party-pays lesson wording at identical pain level, with a matched neutral-attribution control.
falsification_test.falsification_scenario: No rate difference across attribution wordings vs matched control means who-pays attribution does not transfer to ledger cues. A difference without the matched control is invalid attribution.
falsification_test.throwaway_worktree_probe: Flip one attribution-table entry in a throwaway worktree and verify the rate-comparison gate fires on the flip; a gate that cannot fail is not evidence.
